Rumors suggest Apple will offer MacBook Pro users two distinctly different new machine choices this fall: the M6 MacBook Pro and the all-new MacBook Ultra. Here are the details of the upcoming products.

Both the M6 MacBook Pro and MacBook Ultra will launch this fall, each with its own unique advantages

This fall, Apple is expected to launch two new Macs, both of which will appeal to MacBook Pro users:

  • A MacBook Pro equipped with the M6 chip
  • MacBook Ultra (which may also continue to be called MacBook Pro)

The M6-equipped MacBook Pro is expected to be the successor to last fall's M5 model. It won't offer higher-end chip options, nor will there be any redesign.

However, the M6 could be a more exciting than usual major upgrade, as it will be the first Mac chip manufactured using a 2nm process. If you like the current MacBook Pro's design, with its abundance of ports and outstanding battery life, keeping that design alone could be a selling point.

However, for MacBook Pro users looking for something more distinctive, the MacBook Ultra might be just what you're looking for.

The rumored Apple Ultra model will feature a brand-new industrial design, with a thinner and lighter body, plus an OLED display, touch screen, Dynamic Island, and possibly cellular connectivity options.

The MacBook Ultra won't come with the M6 chip, but will instead be available in M5 Pro and M5 Max versions. However, aside from the chip, anyone looking to experience the most cutting-edge Mac technology will find it in the MacBook Ultra.

Based on Apple's typical Mac launch patterns, we're likely to see the M6 MacBook Pro and MacBook Ultra debut together in late October. However, if you need a new MacBook Pro right now, or are on a budget, Apple's refurbished models or deals on Amazon are your best bet.

Will you consider upgrading your MacBook this fall? Which of the two new models do you lean toward? Let us know in the comments.
